parsedVerdict.reasoning: Most of the module is cohesive. There is one use case per file, every file uses the shared mappers in dtos.ts (toOrderDto/toStockLevelDto), and dependencies come in through domain repository and service ports. The exception is ListStockLevelsUseCase in list-stock-levels-use-case.ts. It is a read-only stock query, yet it declares validateExecute(request: PlaceOrderRequest). That method imports and calls assertExecuteRule, which is exported from place-order-use-case.ts. So the 'customerId is required' check for placing an order now has a second entry point in an unrelated use case. The stock-listing file mixes order-placement validation with stock reporting. The rule's helper is also exported from one use-case file and reached into by another, instead of sitting inside PlaceOrderUseCase or in a shared validation or DTO module. This breaks the module's one-use-case-per-file abstraction and splits concerns. A smaller issue: the 'findById → throw NotFoundError' check is repeated in Cancel, Get and Transition. That pattern is common and acceptable, so it is not counted as the main violation.

violations.message: ListStockLevelsUseCase.validateExecute(request: PlaceOrderRequest) calls assertExecuteRule from place-order-use-case.ts. This mixes order-placement validation into a read-only stock-level query. Remove the method and keep validation inside PlaceOrderUseCase.

assertExecuteRule is exported as a free function from a use-case file, and other use cases reach into it. Order-request validation should be private to PlaceOrderUseCase or moved to a dedicated validation or DTO module, not exposed from a use-case file.
